\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item[] \textit{Note:} $\rho = 1$ is log preferences. Panel A: the derivative of the political objective of the electorate of 1990 in the design it chooses for 2020, eq.\ \eqref{eq:esc:leadFOC}, at the U.S.\ choice $\theta_{2020} = 0.544$, by route: the design with the share of revenue lost and the anticipated tax held, which pulls the design towards flat benefits; the dependence of the share lost on the design (eq.\ \eqref{eq:esc:ftheta}), the saving on the loss; and the response of the anticipated tax $\mathcal{T}_{2020}(\theta_{2020})$. The routes sum to zero at the choice; each share is one of the last two routes over their sum, which offsets the pull. Panel B: $\theta_{2020}$ on the path where the choice binds from the first period, as France\textquotesingle s income distribution is imposed on the U.S., first everywhere but in the cost, whose share of revenue lost at each design is held at its U.S.\ value, then in the dispersion of relative incomes $\tilde{V}$ in the cost, and last in the tax rate in the cost; the total is the response to France\textquotesingle s income distribution in figure \ref{fig:US_ESC:overview}, and the split depends on the order of the steps. Under CRRA preferences the share held is met to a relative gap of at most 0.15\%. The dispersion in the cost alone is the U.S.\ with France\textquotesingle s $\tilde{V}$ in the cost, computed under log preferences only. Panel C: the magnitudes of appendix \ref{app:esc:cost}, $\pi = \Pi/R$ on the path without the cost, $\bar{t} = \tau(1-\pi)$ the wedge in place of eq.\ \eqref{eq:esc:wedge} at the calibrated tax rate, $\lambda$ of table \ref{table:US_ESC:calibration}, and $\varepsilon(\bar{t}) = \kappa\bar{t} = \lambda\tau/(2\pi)$ the local elasticity of the base under $\lambda = 2\kappa\pi(1-\pi)$. $\lambda$ at $\varepsilon$ is the cost parameter that a local elasticity $\varepsilon$ implies, $2\pi\varepsilon/\tau$, at the ends of the range of participation and taxable-income elasticities \parencite{ChettyGMW11a1,SaezSG12a1}, and the multiples are the calibrated $\lambda$ over it. Earnings outside the base: the share $\frac{1}{2}\kappa\bar{t}^{2}$ that the wedge in place keeps outside. Fiscal externality: the budget charged with the participation tax of every unit of base that leaves, $\lambda = 3\kappa\pi(1-\pi)$.
\end{tablenotes}
